# temps_deployment (Resource)

Deploys a pre-built Docker image from a registry to an environment of a project (`POST /projects/{id}/environments/{env}/deploy/image`), and by default waits until Temps reports the deployment completed.

Each change of `image`, `command`, `health_check_path` or `triggers` starts a new deployment, which replaces the previous one in the environment once it passes its health check. A deployment that fails is reported with Temps' classified cause and kept in state as tainted, so the next apply deploys again.

Destroying this resource only removes it from state: the deployment keeps serving until another deployment replaces it, so a replacement never stops the environment first. Remove the project or environment to stop it. A deployment made outside Terraform (from the console, CI or a rollback) shows as `is_current = false` and is not undone.

Cannot be imported.

Required API key permissions: `deployments:read`, `deployments:create`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "temps_project" "web" {
  name        = "web"
  source_type = "docker_image"
  preset      = "dockerfile"
}

data "temps_environment" "production" {
  project_id = temps_project.web.id
  name       = "production"
}

# Changing image (or triggers) deploys again; the new deployment replaces
# the running one once it is healthy.
resource "temps_deployment" "web" {
  project_id        = temps_project.web.id
  environment_id    = data.temps_environment.production.id
  image             = "ghcr.io/example-org/web:1.4.2"
  health_check_path = "/healthz"

  timeouts {
    create = "20m"
  }
}

output "web_url" {
  value = temps_deployment.web.url
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (Number) ID of an environment of `project_id`.
- `image` (String) Image reference, for example `ghcr.io/example-org/app:1.4.2`. Pin a tag or a digest (`...@sha256:...`): a moving tag such as `latest` is only pulled again when something here changes (use `triggers`).
- `project_id` (Number) ID of the project.

### Optional

- `command` (List of String) Container command, one argv element per entry, with no shell parsing. Omit it to use the project's saved command, or the image's.
- `health_check_path` (String) HTTP path Temps probes once the container starts, and the environment's uptime monitor checks, for example `/healthz`. Omit it to use the project's saved path, or `/`.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `triggers` (Map of String) Arbitrary values that start a new deployment when they change, for example a build number or the digest a moving tag points at.
- `wait_for_completion` (Boolean) Wait until the deployment completes, failing the apply if it fails. `false` returns once Temps accepted it. Changing it does not deploy again. Defaults to `true`.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the deployment was created (RFC 3339).
- `finished_at` (String) When the deployment finished (RFC 3339), if it has.
- `id` (String) Numeric deployment ID.
- `is_current` (Boolean) Whether this is the environment's current deployment. `false` once another deployment replaced it.
- `status` (String) Deployment status: `pending`, `running`, `built`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, ...
- `url` (String) URL the deployment is served at.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
